sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Current is an electrical/solar EPC contractor with newly commissioned owned power assets, not a demonstrated compounder. A recovered five-year revenue history supports 23.37 percent CAGR, rather than relying only on the stronger three-year window. Cash remains the principal weakness: FY2023–26 CFO is negative each year, and ₹7.11 crore of reported March cash consists of cheques in hand rather than settled bank funds. The linked model distinguishes those claims, existing solar assets and required working-capital finance. At the ₹90 observed close, conditional base returns exceed a 15 percent hurdle but bear loss and poor tradability substantially reduce attractiveness. Numeric scores are conditional research judgments, not transaction instructions. [S1][S2][S5][S7][S11]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: As of October 20, 2026: Current Infraprojects Limited, INE1CRQ01014, NSE SME CURRENT, listed September 3, 2025. Actual shares 19,148,000 and lot 1,600 are verified against annual capital and the traded SM security master. October 19 close ₹90 was one trade, not an executable bid. Scope is consolidated Indian GAAP/AS with the same parent standalone history before newly formed subsidiaries; it is not assumed to be Ind AS because of isolated template references. G1 Integrity, G2 Reliability, G3 Funding and G4 Tradability are Conditional. Five-year horizon, 15 percent nominal pre-tax shareholder return hurdle and ₹5 lakh reference position are analyst conventions, not suitability advice. Historical and model confidence is medium overall; cheque settlement and live depth remain unverified, with bounded sensitivities rather than silently assumed cash. [S1][S2][S5][S23]

sections.title: Scorecard & Factor Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.04; GQS 5.00, capped at 5 for persistent CASH weakness; conditional IAS 4.81. Factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 6, R 7, D 3, P 4 and L 1. REV selects the preferred five-year 23.37 percent history, not the 38.05 percent three-year rate. Base IRR 18.30 percent produces R 7 against the 15 percent hurdle. Cash and current power-revenue sensitivities do not automatically invalidate the whole valuation: separately eliminating cheque recovery or reducing full-year power revenue to ₹4.5 crore keeps R in the same band. Larger combined operating/funding stresses are reflected in D/P, not hidden by a favorable point estimate. Full arithmetic, caps, evidence and confidence accompany the record. [S1][S2][S7][S14][S15]

sections.title: Business Model & Industry Position
sections.text: EPC work spans electrical, solar, water and civil contracts. FY2026 consolidated revenue of ₹160.39 crore includes ₹156.45 crore EPC, ₹0.43 crore rent, ₹0.63 crore unbilled revenue and ₹2.88 crore power generation. Parent revenue ₹170.23 crore is higher because intercompany EPC is eliminated in the group; it must not be mixed with consolidated debt/profit. Four newly formed solar SPVs built the owned RESCO platform, rather than importing a large purchased revenue base. Owned power shifts economics from project execution to capital, irradiation, availability, PPA collection and debt service. KPI Green is a larger IPP/CPP comparator, while Ganesh Green is adjacent solar/electrical/water EPC with manufacturing differences. Their broader portfolios and financing preclude mechanically importing margins or stock multiples. [S1][S2][S25][S26]

sections.title: Moat & Competitive Advantage
sections.text: In-house MEC testing, project qualifications, procurement and execution relationships can reduce delivery friction. They are not a verified monopoly or persistent pricing advantage. FY2025 largest customer represented 26.65 percent and top ten 81.82 percent of revenue; contractor costs were about 40 percent of cost of goods sold. Geographic concentration in Rajasthan, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh adds policy and execution exposure. The prospectus reports 18 delayed completions out of 87 projects, with management stating no damages or cancellation for those delays; this is more nuanced than a later general statement that there had been no large delays. Current external awards validate customer access, not an independently reconciled backlog or competitive moat. [S2][S12][S13][S20][S21][S22]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Earnings Quality
sections.text: Revenue FY2021–26 is ₹56.11, ₹60.72, ₹60.96, ₹77.57, ₹90.88 and ₹160.39 crore. Preferred five-year CAGR is 23.37 percent, versus 38.05 percent over three years. FY2025–26 includes greenfield solar subsidiaries with internal work eliminated, so consolidated external revenue is the appropriate economic comparison. Price/volume and contract-mix detail remain limited, but no material purchased business is required to explain the growth. Prospectus restated FY2023/24 PAT is ₹1.4924/₹5.0892 crore, versus small differences in original director summaries; this is not itself adverse economics. FY2026 PAT ₹14.0518 crore divided by current shares gives about ₹7.34 per share, not the ₹8.31 weighted-average EPS. Operating EBITDA excluding ₹0.9619 crore other income is ₹23.2259 crore. Solar straight-line depreciation is disclosed; a full-year depreciation burden is included in the model rather than extrapolating partial-year plant charges. [S1][S2][S7][S8][S9]

sections.title: Runway, Reinvestment & Capital Allocation
sections.text: The 9.4 MW owned plants are commissioned and already in opening PPE. Management’s annual levelized revenue above ₹6 crore is tested against ₹4.5–6.5 crore scenarios, not treated as audited output. Three solar term loans total ₹20.40 crore at a disclosed 10.4 percent rate and 15-year tenure. An illustrative ₹6 crore revenue/80 percent cash-margin case yields modest unlevered returns after full depreciation and tax, so recurring income alone does not prove superior capital allocation. EPC continues to need working capital and replacement assets. September/October awards include ₹10.42 crore, ₹44.76 crore including taxes/charges, and two BSF awards of ₹4.89/₹4.03 crore. Do not add these indiscriminately to the annual ₹305 crore backlog label, which itself carries a later May-award footnote. July banks sanctioned enhanced combined fund/nonfund limits, not unrestricted cash. Proposed BESS/expansion has no invented profit; a ₹20 crore cash-only sensitivity tests an unproductive deployment. [S1][S2][S14][S15][S20][S21][S22]

sections.title: Governance & Minority Shareholder Protection
sections.text: Promoter-family control, remuneration and subsidiary transactions require normal minority safeguards. Family salaries disclosed total ₹0.96 crore and related rent ₹0.1772 crore; group eliminations prevent treating intercompany EPC/loans as automatic leakage. The May 26, 2026 signed IPO-use statement reports that ₹27 lakh originally allocated to Dhanbad subsidiary equity was used for working capital instead, with shareholder approval marked No. The issuer explains that subsidiary investment required ₹558 lakh rather than ₹585 lakh, while working-capital utilization increased from ₹3,000 lakh to ₹3,027 lakh. The reallocation is about 0.70 percent of ₹3,854.48 lakh net proceeds. It is a disclosed governance/compliance matter, not evidence by itself of diversion or a critical failure of the financial statements. A general call statement that funds were used as intended is less precise than the signed variation table and does not erase it. July filings show the existing CEO Chetan Dadhich joining the board as whole-time director, not replacement of the CEO. Promoter market purchases add to promoter holdings but do not raise issuer cash or change total shares. September AGM authorities include up to ₹200 crore subsidiary transactions and ₹150 crore Section 186 assistance; these ceilings are not actual transfers. Unmodified audit and secretarial reports do not provide blanket integrity assurance, while minor incorporation/year-label errors do not alone justify an integrity failure. [S1][S2][S11][S12][S17][S18][S19]

sections.title: Financial Forensics & Cash Conversion
sections.text: Restated FY2023–25 CFO is −₹0.2640, −₹0.4343 and −₹1.1037 crore; FY2026 CFO is −₹9.2032 crore. Four-year CFO totals −₹11.01 crore against ₹30.09 crore PAT, a persistent cash-quality issue. FY2026 receivables, inventories and advances absorb cash before ₹20.8479 crore capex; CFO minus capex is −₹30.0511 crore. The reported financing/investing/operating bridge reconciles the ₹7.361 crore cash increase, but note 16 reveals ₹7.1149 crore cheques in hand and only ₹0.389 crore bank/cash. This qualification changes available liquidity, not the arithmetical cash-flow total. Restricted FDs of ₹6.4069 crore and ₹0.553 crore escrow are excluded from free cash. Unsecured financial loans ₹3.02 crore have separate recovery sensitivities. Undisputed receivables over one year total ₹5.5773 crore; the report also describes legacy IL&FS-related claims and partial bad-debt charges, so aged balances are not called fully recovered. ₹2.6172 crore TReDS is financing. The ₹21 crore subsidiary guarantee overlaps debt already consolidated and is not added twice. Latest CARO disputed GST/tax is about ₹0.157 crore; old IPO proceedings are not assumed still wholly outstanding or silently cleared. [S1][S2][S11][S12][S13]

sections.title: Valuation & Scenario Returns
sections.text: ₹90 times 19,148,000 shares implies ₹172.332 crore equity value and 12.26 times current-share FY2026 earnings. Enterprise value is about ₹204.99 crore using settled bank/cash only, versus ₹197.87 crore if every cheque is treated as cash; this distinction is explicit, not a hidden valuation choice. The full model links EPC revenue/margin, existing solar output, actual opening WC of ₹60.9098 crore, maintenance capex, depreciation, tax, scheduled term principal and circular average-debt interest. Base assumptions are EPC growth 15 percent, margin 13 percent, WC 40 percent of EPC revenue, power revenue ₹6 crore at 80 percent cash margin, and terminal multiples 8 times EPC/9 times power EBITDA. No repeat IPO proceeds or new equity rescue is assumed. Results: bear: terminal ₹38.85, five-year IRR -15.47%, peak debt ₹55.66 crore; base: terminal ₹208.52, five-year IRR 18.30%, peak debt ₹25.00 crore; bull: terminal ₹439.32, five-year IRR 37.31%, peak debt ₹18.92 crore. Sixteen sensitivities vary cheque recovery/timing, WC, power output, optional unfunded expansion, margin and multiples. Base total debt stays below the ₹33.04 crore opening balance; severe refinancing is not assumed committed. Restricted/legacy assets have conditional recovery, not opening spending power. These are estimates, not probabilities or verified bounds; the supported base spread is scored while substantial loss and estimation risk are separately reflected in D/P. [S1][S5][S11][S14][S15] Opening-claim review, 20 October 2026: no omitted opening cash claim was identified in the reviewed consolidated balance-sheet notes. Net tax ₹2.5293 crore is paid once; statutory dues, employee/director accruals, customer advances, audit accrual, current and long retention payables and gratuity are already included in net operating working capital. Retention/security assets are included there once. Restricted deposits, escrow and financial loans have separate conditional terminal recovery; cheques are collected separately, not counted twice as debtors. Existing solar debt and current maturities are included in the financing schedule. No numerical model change was made.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Map
sections.text: The bear case is collection-led: stagnant EPC revenue, 9 percent margin, 55 percent WC intensity, reduced power output, delayed/partial cheque settlement and higher WC interest. It gives ₹38.85 terminal value versus ₹90, with peak debt about ₹55.66 crore. Severe stress adds a 15 percent noncash WC impairment and replacement funding once, zero cheque recovery, lower execution and a historical-tax cash sensitivity, yielding about ₹14.84 with peak debt ₹61.42 crore. The old tax stress is illustrative, not an assertion every IPO claim remains open. A bank-guarantee call could add risk but all guarantees are not assumed to crystallize automatically. Funding difficulty, dilution, debtor write-offs or unproductive optional expansion can create permanent loss; a falling quotation alone is not the thesis. [S1][S2][S14][S15]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold/tenfold from ₹90 means ₹450/₹900 and annualized appreciation of 37.97/58.49 percent over five years. With all other base assumptions fixed, linked revenue/funding hurdles require EPC CAGR of 41.69/66.66 percent. These are algebraic requirements, not forecasts. Even the combined bull scenario gives about ₹439, slightly below fivefold. Sustainable cash-funded growth and per-share economics, not commissioning announcements or a large headline opportunity, determine feasibility. No 10× probability is assigned. [S1][S5]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Verify cheque clearance and subsequent collection bank evidence; next interim results should show whether CFO improves and aged receivables decline. Reconcile actual power generation, tariffs, operating expenses and loan principal against the existing 9.4 MW plants. Obtain bank fund/nonfund splits, current drawings and conditions-precedent completion before assuming stress funding. Track remaining backlog net of execution and cancellations, retaining tax-inclusive versus accounting-revenue distinctions. Follow the ₹27 lakh IPO reallocation’s compliance resolution proportionately. Review unsecured-loan counterparties/recovery and current tax appeal status, not only accounting earnings. Update promoter encumbrances, actual share issues and trade-time depth. Persistent collection deterioration, unexplained related deployment or an unfunded expansion would weaken the case; an immaterial corrected label alone would not. [S1][S11][S14][S15][S20][S21][S22][S24]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Cash-conversion and execution-sensitive EPC/RESCO watchlist with moderate business quality and low conditional investment attractiveness after downside and implementation risk. The initial screen’s history, scope and opening-WC gaps are substantially resolved; bounded cheque/operating uncertainties are tested rather than used as blanket reasons to avoid all scoring. Numeric IAS remains conditional on the stated model, price and ₹5 lakh reference test, not a personalized entry recommendation. All gates are Conditional, and live implementation remains especially constrained by large lot size and sparse turnover. [S1][S2][S5][S7][S14][S15][S24]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary review now extends from FY2021 comparison/FY2022–24 original reports through prospectus FY2023–25 restated accounts and FY2026 parent/group statements. Greenfield subsidiary formation and group sales eliminations resolve the earlier constant-scope concern sufficiently for the preferred five-year growth score. Refresh covers April rating, May proceeds statement and results, two earnings calls, June/July promoter purchases, July bank sanctions/board change, September AGM and October awards/certificates. No interim FY2027 financial outcome is invented. Remaining uncertainties are cheque settlement, current customer/loan recovery, detailed loan calendar and fund-based headroom, plant output/collections, latest encumbrances and live trading depth. Specific sensitivities show their consequences; source confidence and assumptions remain visible. Peer comparison is qualitative, without unverified current market-share or multiple rankings. [S1][S2][S7][S8][S9][S10][S11][S12][S13][S14][S15][S17][S18][S19][S20][S21][S22][S25][S26][S27]

GOV.reason: Promoter control and broad subsidiary assistance need monitoring. IPO reallocation is explicitly disclosed, about 0.70 percent of net proceeds, not proof of diversion. Reporting mistakes and a general call statement do not override the signed specific disclosure; safeguards remain conditional.

MOAT.reason: Testing/qualification, tender history and execution capability offer some differentiation, but customer concentration, subcontracting and competitive bidding constrain durable pricing power.

REV.reason: Preferred five-year reported comparable-business CAGR is 23.37 percent, starting band 8. Three-year 38.05 percent is shown but not selected opportunistically. Subsidiaries are greenfield owned plants, with internal EPC eliminated; no acquired revenue distortion or unearned TAM uplift.

DUR.reason: Electrical and solar tender flow plus commissioned owned power provide evidenced runway. Renewals, policy, customer concentration and collection risk prevent a high-certainty long-duration score.

CAP.reason: EPC economics and scaling are attractive conditionally, while newly commissioned capital depresses incremental returns and power economics depend on actual output. Illustrative 6 crore power revenue at 80 percent cash margin less depreciation/tax yields only around 7–8 percent unlevered return on installed cost, not automatic superior ROIC.

CASH.reason: Four consecutive negative reported operating-cash years despite profit, rising aging and 7.11 crore unsettled cheques demonstrate persistent weak realization. Retention classification and capex are distinguished, not double penalized.

BAL.reason: IPO-funded equity and existing bank sanctions support base funding; modeled base total debt declines below opening debt. Restricted balances and cheques are not free cash. Bear/severe cases require materially more WC borrowing, and cash headroom is not independently confirmed.

EXEC.reason: Commissioned 9.4 MW, strong external EPC growth and new awards evidence delivery. Prospectus records 18 delayed projects out of 87, reportedly without damages; collection performance and reporting need improvement. A call denial of large delays is not accepted as a clean historical record.

EARN.reason: Profit growth mainly operating rather than other income, but IPO dilution and solar depreciation/ramp mean current-share EPS is below weighted EPS. Restated versus original small tax/profit differences are disclosed; cash weakness is separately scored.

R.reason: Conditional base five-year IRR 18.30 percent less 15 percent hurdle gives +3.30 percentage points, canonical band 7. Zero cheque recovery and a lower 4.5 crore full-year power-revenue case separately retain the same R band; no probability weighting is invented.

D.reason: Bear terminal price 38.85 versus 90 and severe 14.84 imply material permanent-loss exposure; peak debt rises to 55.66/61.42 crore. Additional lending availability and guarantees are not presumed. No verified current default.

P.reason: A fair execution case exceeds the hurdle, but linked margin/multiple sensitivities can reduce modeled return near zero; several operating and valuation assumptions must hold together. Price is not demonstrably robust to modest estimation errors.

L.reason: Both observed-only and conditional-zero calendars imply over 20 days at 5 percent participation; one lot is 28.8 percent of the 5 lakh reference position. Latest single trade, concentrated PAN activity and unknown depth make implementation especially fragile.

valuation.opening_WC_formula: 23.5648 inventory + 52.15 receivables + 11.7412 short advances - 3.02 unsecured financial loans + 5.8989 other current assets - 0.553 escrow - 0.0037 preliminary expense + 4.1622 long retention/security - 17.0778 trade payables - 13.2688 other current liabilities - 2.3894 long retention payable - 0.2616 gratuity - 0.033 audit accrual = 60.9098
methodology: Actual consolidated March balances, not forecast ratios, anchor opening operating WC. Intragroup EPC and loans are eliminated; parent revenue is not combined with group debt. Subsidiary minority interests are economically immaterial but no separately invented minority profit is added.

Reported cash 7.5039 includes 7.1149 cheques in hand. Only bank/cash 0.389 is opening spendable cash. Realization is a separate cash receipt, not new revenue or a second reduction of debtors; failed realization is noncash impairment with no second cash payment. Clearance timing/recovery remain unverified and explicitly stressed.

IPO proceeds were already received and used before opening. No repeat IPO cash, future issue or warrant dilution is assumed. Current 19,148,000 shares are preserved; changes in authorized capital and promoter market purchases are not new issuer funding.

Existing 9.4 MW power plants are already funded in PPE and are not bought again. Full-year power revenue 4.5/6/6.5 crore tests management’s 6-plus crore levelized revenue claim; output, irradiation, curtailment and collection are not independently certified. Power cash margin, depreciation and maintenance assumptions are explicit.

EPC/other revenue is actual consolidated total less power revenue. Operating margins by module are assumptions because audited segment EBITDA is not supplied. Future power depreciation uses gross cost 35.0929 crore times 3.8 percent; EPC depreciation uses 25 percent of opening smaller asset base plus half new capex. Tax benefits from impairments are not assumed.

Term principal amortizes the actual 20.4025 crore solar loan, first year 1.4844 crore current maturities and then 1/15 of initial principal as an explicit illustrative schedule. Actual detailed bank repayment calendar may differ. Working-capital borrowing separately bridges the cash floor, including refinancing principal if operations are insufficient.

Interest uses average opening/closing term and WC debt, solving new-draw circularity. Sanctioned fund/nonfund facilities are not treated as fully available cash; new modeled borrowing is a required amount, not a verified commitment or disbursement.

Restricted FD and escrow are excluded from spendable opening cash; only conditional terminal release is included. Unsecured financial loans 3.02 crore are excluded from operating WC and have conditional terminal recovery. No other-income interest is extrapolated into operating EBITDA.

Noncash WC impairment reduces usable opening assets and replacement funding is charged once. Historical tax-demand stress 2.0918 crore is illustrative from IPO significant proceedings, not a claim all remain outstanding or an addition to smaller latest disclosed disputes. No loss on all bank guarantees is assumed without an actual call.

Optional 20 crore new-expansion sensitivity has no invented profits or terminal asset recovery. It tests funding drain, not an identified committed BESS project. No operating WC or PPE is added twice to terminal EV.

Five-year terminal value uses separate EPC and power EBITDA multiples, not a perpetuity beyond PPA/asset life. Dividends are zero. Scenarios are analytical estimates with sensitivities, not verified bounds or a guarantee of finance and execution.
